metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes — GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 has a real plan mode (`--plan` / `--mode plan`, shift+tab, mode-tinted TUI) whose approval overlay offers Accept-on-autopilot / Accept-interactive / exit_only, driven by a genuine model-invocable builtin tool named `exit_plan_mode`. daemon_capability: bug — PROBED RED through the production tailer: an open `exit_plan_mode` tool call yields NeedsUserAttention=false, IsAgentDone=false, IsWaitingForUserInput=false, so the session sits in `working` for the entire time the user is blocked on the plan overlay; the SAME probe with the claudecode spelling `ExitPlanMode` returns NeedsUserAttention=true, so the whole defect is a missing snake_case entry in isUserBlockingTool (core/domain/session/metrics.go:450) and its twin tailer.isUserBlockingToolName. driver_capability: gap:plan-mode-launch — plan mode is entered only by a launch flag (`--plan`) or the shift+tab mode cycle; there is no /plan slash command in the 1.0.77 bundle, and driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl has no lever to add a launch flag.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: **yes** — Copilot CLI 1.0.77 ships a first-class plan mode with an ExitPlanMode-equivalent approval gate.
daemon_capability: **bug** — the trace exists and is persisted, but irrlichd never leaves `working`. PROBED RED through the production tailer.
driver_capability: **gap:plan-mode-launch** — the copilot driver cannot start the REPL in plan mode.

## agent — plan mode is real, and its gate is a tool

The shipped 1.0.77 bundle registers three session modes (`interactive`, `autopilot`, `plan` — `sessionConstantsSessionModes()`), exposes them as `--mode <mode>` with `--plan` and `--autopilot` shorthands (all three mutually `conflicts()`-ed), tints the TUI per mode (`modePlan` / `modePlanSoft` theme tokens, the `"user prompt in plan mode"` timeline sample) and gates writes behind `isPlanModeWriteGateActive()`. Every prompt sent while `currentMode==="plan"` is rewritten to `[[PLAN]] <prompt>` by `applyPlanAndModeAdjustments`.

The approval gate is the direct ExitPlanMode analogue the scenario asks for. `iU="exit_plan_mode"` is a **model-invocable builtin tool**, registered through the same `AT(name, execute, summarise)` → `Wo(descriptor, …)` factory as `bash` / `ask_user`, and it is present in the tool array only while in plan mode (`Kn && this.currentMode!=="plan" && (T = T.filter(ut => ut.name !== iU))`). When the model calls it, `toolExitPlanModeExecute` awaits a registered callback; the TUI enqueues an overlay whose actions are exactly `{autopilot: "Accept plan and build on autopilot", autopilot_fleet: "…on autopilot + /fleet", interactive: "Accept plan and build on default permissions", exit_only: "Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself"}`. The agent is blocked until one is chosen — structurally identical to claudecode's ExitPlanMode overlay.

## daemon — the trace IS persisted, and the daemon still misses it

Two emission facts, read at the seam:

1. The **request** is ephemeral and therefore invisible on disk. `exit_plan_mode.requested` is published via `this.emitEphemeral(...)` from `applyInputRequested` when `e.inputKind==="exitPlanMode"`, exactly like `user_input.requested` and unlike `permission.requested`. So the 2-19 transcript-tier permission rule cannot fire here, and neither can any request-shaped signal.
2. The **tool call** is NOT ephemeral. Tool execution runs through the native model-stream planner, whose generic `case "emit_tool_execution_start"` action does `this.emit("tool.execution_start", …)` with `{toolCallId, toolName, arguments}` for every tool request in the stream. `exit_plan_mode` is an ordinary entry in that stream, so `tool.execution_start` with `toolName:"exit_plan_mode"` lands in `events.jsonl` and stays open (no `tool.execution_complete`) for the whole time the overlay is held.

That is a real trace, and the daemon mis-handles it. A throwaway probe (written into `core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot`, run, deleted — no repo change) drove a plan-mode 1.0.77 sequence through the PRODUCTION tailer (`tailer.NewTranscriptTailer(path, &Parser{}, AdapterName)`) and then through the domain predicates the classifier calls:

```
LastEventType="function_call" HasOpenToolCall=true LastOpenToolNames=[exit_plan_mode] TranscriptPermissionPending=false
NeedsUserAttention=false  IsAgentDone=false  IsWaitingForUserInput=false
with PascalCase ExitPlanMode: NeedsUserAttention=true
```

The chain, each seam read:

1. **Parse.** `parseToolStart` (parser.go:212) sets `ev.EventType="function_call"` and `ev.ToolUses=[{ID, Name:"exit_plan_mode"}]`.
2. **Fold.** `tailer_metrics.go:469-475` sets `HasOpenToolCall=true`, `LastOpenToolNames=["exit_plan_mode"]`, and `TranscriptPermissionPending=false` (no `permission.requested` — plan approval is not a permission).
3. **Derive.** `NeedsUserAttention()` (metrics.go:424) walks `LastOpenToolNames` through `isUserBlockingTool` (metrics.go:450), an EXACT-match list of `AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / question / ask_user_question`. `exit_plan_mode` is not in it → false. `IsAgentDone()` returns false because the open-tool guard fires first.
4. **Classify.** No hook tier (copilot installs none), `transcript_permission_prompt` false, `agent_done` false, `NeedsUserAttention` false → the default "transcript activity → working" rule wins. **The session shows `working` while the user stares at an approval overlay** — a false-busy, the exact inverse of the false-ready the sibling 2-17 caveat describes.

The last probe line is the load-bearing one: swap the tool name for claudecode's `ExitPlanMode` spelling and the same metrics return `NeedsUserAttention=true`. Nothing else about the arc is missing — no new parser field, no new event kind. **The fix is adding `exit_plan_mode` to `isUserBlockingTool` and to its twin `tailer.isUserBlockingToolName`** (the two are documented as KEEP-IN-SYNC, with twin tests `TestNeedsUserAttention_UserBlockingToolNames` and `TestIsUserBlockingToolName`). The list already carries snake_case entries for vibe (`ask_user_question`), so this is the established shape, not a new mechanism. That is a spec-required observable the daemon mis-handles on an existing trace → `bug`, not `incapable`, and not a caveat.

The spec below is therefore written to assert the CORRECT arc (`ready → working → waiting`) and marked `known_failing`, so the recording documents the defect rather than blessing it.

## driver — plan mode has no in-REPL entry point

The 1.0.77 slash-command registry contains no `/plan` and no generic `/mode` (enumerating the command-name constants yields `/model /autopilot /agent /new /clear /resume /compact …` — `/autopilot on|off` toggles only autopilot↔interactive). Plan mode is entered by **`copilot --plan`** (or `--mode plan`), both confirmed in the live `copilot --help` output, or by the shift+tab mode cycle.

`replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh`'s `launch_repl` builds `local args=(--no-color)` plus three fixed env levers (`COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL`, `COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS`, `RESUME_ID`) and has no lever for the agent mode, so the recipe cannot be driven as written. This is TOOLING, not observability: the port is one line beside the existing `COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL` guard —

```sh
[[ -n "${COPILOT_PLAN_MODE:-}" ]] && args+=(--plan)
```

— exactly the shape 2-19 already established for its own launch-config need. The shift+tab route was considered and rejected as the recipe's mechanism: `keys` IS in `DRIVE_ELICITS` and would send `S-Tab` fine, but the bundle does not expose the cycle order, so "one press lands on plan" cannot be asserted from evidence, and a mode-cycle miss would silently record an interactive-mode session that never emits `exit_plan_mode` at all. The launch flag is deterministic and documented on the live surface.

## Why the recipe keeps --allow-all

Unlike 2-19, this cell WANTS the permission system silent. In plan mode the write gate would otherwise fire `permission.requested` for any edit attempt, which drives `waiting` through the 2-19 transcript-permission rule and would mask the very defect this cell exists to document. With `--allow-all` no `permission.requested` is ever written, so the only thing that can move this session out of `working` is the `exit_plan_mode` tool — making the recording a clean, single-variable witness of the bug, and a clean witness of the fix once the tool name is added.
caveats: PROVISIONAL — EMISSION, not parsing. That `tool.execution_start` carries `toolName:"exit_plan_mode"` is read from the 1.0.77 bundle (the generic `emit_tool_execution_start` planner action → `this.emit("tool.execution_start", {toolCallId, toolName, arguments})`, driven off the model stream's tool request), not from a live capture — no copilot recording with a plan-mode turn exists yet. The daemon-side half IS proven (the probe above ran the production tailer). If a live run shows Copilot special-cases exit_plan_mode out of the tool stream and only publishes the ephemeral `exit_plan_mode.requested`, the pillar must be corrected to `incapable` and this cell frozen — that is the single thing `record` most needs to check, and the reason confidence is 0.8 rather than 0.9.

The approval REQUEST and its resolution are unobservable regardless. `exit_plan_mode.requested` and `exit_plan_mode.completed` are both `emitEphemeral` (the same class as `user_input.requested`, which the 2-17 sibling established is provably absent from events.jsonl), so the plan text, the offered actions and which action the user picked never reach the transcript. What IS observable, post-fix, is the state arc — waiting while the tool is open, working again on `tool.execution_complete` — which is exactly what the scenario's acceptance criteria assert. The one exception: choosing "Accept and build on autopilot" (or exit_only) writes a NON-ephemeral `session.mode_changed {previousMode:"plan", newMode:"autopilot"|"interactive"}`, so the mode flip itself is on disk; the copilot parser currently Skips that event type (it falls through parser.go's default arm), which is correct for state but means the mode is not surfaced anywhere.

The recipe deliberately never answers the overlay, so the `waiting → working → ready` return leg of the scenario's process is NOT exercised — same as the claudecode and codex siblings, whose acceptance criteria also terminate at `Final state: waiting`.

UNVERIFIED whether `--allow-all` (or the AUTO_APPROVAL feature flag) can auto-resolve the plan overlay. The bundle's auto-approval path (`j$=Je.AUTO_APPROVAL===!0`) is a server-side feature flag and is not obviously wired to `--allow-all-tools`, and the overlay is a client prompt rather than a permission, so it should still be held — but if the recording shows the plan being auto-accepted, re-run with `COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1` and accept that a plan-mode write gate may fire `permission.requested` first (which would satisfy the state assertion via the 2-19 rule while leaving THIS cell's mechanism unproven — flag that as a partial, do not bless it).

PROVISIONAL — BIRTH SHAPE (emission, not parsing). Modeled as a PRESESSION adapter, matching the 2-1, 2-17 and 2-19 copilot siblings: the driver's SEAM-3 comment records that Copilot creates the session-state directory at launch but writes events.jsonl only once the first turn starts, so the `copilot` process (ExactName matcher) is discoverable before any transcript exists and a transient proc-<PID> row precedes the real session (whose id is the DIRECTORY name via sessionIDFromPath). Only a live capture settles it; if the recording shows a single birth, `record` must re-anchor.

OBSERVATIONS assert `agent` only, matching the 2-19 sibling: the run terminates mid-turn in waiting, before any `assistant.turn_end` / `session.usage_checkpoint` / `session.shutdown`. Per-message `assistant.message.outputTokens` will probably have landed by then (the tool call rides an assistant message), so tokens may well be non-zero — but asserting it would be a guess about whether Copilot emits a text-bearing assistant.message for a tool-only reply, and a wrong non-zero assertion fails every recording. MODEL is left unpinned deliberately: the account backing these recordings exposes only gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 and the effective model is resolved at runtime and announced by session.auto_mode_resolved.

sources.note: Shipped CLI 1.0.77 bundle (compressed Node SEA — `strings` on the launcher yields nothing, this is the readable artifact). Evidence used: `iU="exit_plan_mode"` with `rG="interactive" oU="autopilot" cde="autopilot_fleet"`; `Sgt()` registering it via `AT(iU, execute, summarise)` → `Wo(descriptor,…)`, the same builtin factory as bash/ask_user; the plan-mode-only tool filter `Kn && this.currentMode!=="plan" && (T=T.filter(ut=>ut.name!==iU))`; the overlay action labels {autopilot, autopilot_fleet, interactive, exit_only}; `applyInputRequested`'s `e.inputKind==="exitPlanMode" → this.emitEphemeral("exit_plan_mode.requested", …)` (contrast `permission.requested`, emitted via this.emit); the generic planner action `case "emit_tool_execution_start": … this.emit("tool.execution_start", ms)`; `set currentMode` emitting NON-ephemeral `session.mode_changed`; `applyPlanAndModeAdjustments` prefixing `[[PLAN]] `; and the absence of any `/plan` or `/mode` entry in the slash-command name constants.

`--mode <mode>  Set the initial agent mode (choices: "interactive", "plan", "autopilot")` and `--plan  Start in plan mode`. The live surface confirming the deterministic entry point the recipe uses; also `--autopilot`, and shift+tab documented in-TUI as "switch modes".

isUserBlockingTool (line 450) exact-matches AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / question / ask_user_question — `exit_plan_mode` is absent, which is the whole defect; NeedsUserAttention (line 424) walks LastOpenToolNames through it; IsAgentDone's open-tool guard is what keeps the session in `working` rather than settling it to ready. The doc comment names tailer.isUserBlockingToolName as the KEEP-IN-SYNC twin and TestNeedsUserAttention_UserBlockingToolNames / TestIsUserBlockingToolName as the pinning tests.

parseToolStart (line 212) maps tool.execution_start → EventType "function_call" + ToolUses[{ID,Name}] using data.toolName verbatim, so the snake_case name reaches LastOpenToolNames unchanged. parsePermissionRequested (line 243) is the only path to TranscriptPermissionPending, and plan approval never takes it.
Lines 469-475: HasOpenToolCall / LastOpenToolNames / TranscriptPermissionPending are folded exactly as the probe observed them (open tool, no pending permission).

The rules that could route this to waiting and do not: transcript_permission_prompt (needs TranscriptPermissionPending, false here) and agent_done (needs IsAgentDone, false while a tool is open). With NeedsUserAttention false the default transcript-activity rule wins → working.

launch_repl (line ~179) builds `local args=(--no-color)` plus COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL / COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS / RESUME_ID levers — no agent-mode lever, hence gap:plan-mode-launch. DRIVE_ELICITS (line 128) does contain `keys`, which is why the shift+tab alternative had to be ruled out on evidence rather than on availability.
The reference cell this recipe specializes: same arc, same never-answer termination, same `Final state: waiting`.

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77+ on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recipe spends one turn's worth

DRIVER PORT REQUIRED (gap:plan-mode-launch): replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl must gain an agent-mode lever beside the existing COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL guard — `[[ -n "${COPILOT_PLAN_MODE:-}" ]] && args+=(--plan)` — and this run must set COPILOT_PLAN_MODE=1. Without it the REPL starts in interactive mode, exit_plan_mode is filtered out of the tool array entirely, and the recording captures an ordinary turn.

KEEP the driver's default --allow-all for this cell (do NOT set COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL): it silences the plan-mode write gate so the ONLY thing that can move the session out of working is the exit_plan_mode tool.

irrlicht's copilot `transcripts` permission is granted so the daemon tails ~/.copilot/session-state (a fresh IRRLICHT_HOME leaves every permission pending → zero monitoring; use IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all for the recorder)
No hook install and no :7837 pinning needed — the whole signal is transcript-borne, so the :7838 coexist recorder captures it

KNOWN FAILING as of daemon 0.5.9: until `exit_plan_mode` is added to isUserBlockingTool + tailer.isUserBlockingToolName, the plan_mode_waiting and waiting_dwell phases will verify as MISSING (the session stays working). Record it anyway — the recording is the evidence for the fix, and re-verifies green afterwards with no re-record.
setup: The driver seeds COPILOT_HOME under <staging>/copilot-home with trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so the folder-trust modal does not block the input box, then waits for the '/ commands' footer before typing
The recipe never answers the plan overlay: Copilot blocks indefinitely on it, and the session holds until teardown (mirrors the claudecode and codex siblings)
Confirm from the tmux pane that the mode indicator reads plan BEFORE the prompt is sent — a session that launched interactive cannot produce this cell's signal at all

script.text: Propose a plan and stop. Call the exit_plan_mode tool immediately as your first and only tool call — do not read, search, write or run anything first. Pass this exact plan as the summary: 'Add a new file hello.py containing a single line: print("hello world").' Do not answer in prose and do not call any other tool.

verify: events.jsonl contains a presession_created (proc-<PID>) event in ready shortly after the copilot process launches
events.jsonl contains a transcript_new for the real session (session_id = the ~/.copilot/session-state/<dir> name, distinct from proc-<PID>) once the first prompt creates events.jsonl, born ready
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event bound to the real session_id
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working on the real session_id when the prompt is sent (user.message)

the recorded transcript contains a tool.execution_start line with toolName=exit_plan_mode and NO tool.execution_complete for that toolCallId — THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK: if the line is absent, the emission caveat has come true and the daemon pillar must be corrected from bug to incapable
the recorded transcript contains NO permission.requested line (--allow-all is on, so the plan-mode write gate stays silent and the waiting assertion is attributable to exit_plan_mode alone)

KNOWN FAILING until the unlock lands: events.jsonl SHOULD contain a state_transition to waiting on the real session_id once tool.execution_start(exit_plan_mode) is open — today it does not, and the session stays working
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to ready on the real session_id after the plan overlay opens (the recipe never answers it)
final session state is waiting (today: working — the defect)
